La femme chaſte [?] & pudique, qui aime bien ſon mary:
n'a rien ſi cher ne ſi precieux que ſa preſence, & rien ſi
faſcheux & lamentable que ſon abſcence: teſmoins les

uncertain.note: the page opens mid-word: 'madoüant' is the continuation of 'a-' on p019 (amadoüant). p019 is not transcribed, so the word is read on its own; continues_prev is set true on that basis.

uncertain.note: 'pour quoy' is set with a gap of the same width as the gap in 'la cauſe' on the same line, so it is transcribed as two words. Reader B may read 'pourquoy'. The comma after 'cauſe' is set with a space before it in the print; normalized per §1.

uncertain.note: the marker after 'corps' is a clear small italic n (checked at 12x); it is the only marker of this annotation on the page and fits the alphabet running on from p019. Its note is the first margin note.

uncertain.text: Dont ne faloit ſ'esbahir, ſi la ſuppliãt
uncertain.note: the TEXTE quotation is set in larger type but as running prose, so it is a paragraph block, not headings, following p011/p044. 'faloit' is printed with a single l (sic); 'ſ'esbahir' has long s for the elided pronoun and round s before b, as §2 expects; 'ſuppliãt' carries a tilde over the a.

uncertain.text: La femme chaſte[?] & pudique, qui aime bien ſon mary:
uncertain.note: [?]: a full-height vertical stroke is printed tight between 'chaſte' and '&', running from above x-height to below the baseline, with no dot. It is not any letter of this fount and is too tall for a comma; most likely a damaged comma sort or a piece of spacing material that took ink. Sense wants 'chaſte & pudique' or 'chaſte, & pudique'. Reader B may read a comma, or nothing at all. ESCALATE.

uncertain.note: 'Proteſilaë': two dots are printed over the final e (the left one lightly inked), so a diaeresis is transcribed. At reading size it looks like an acute; reader B may read 'Proteſilaé'.

uncertain.text: ſence duquel elle deploroit tant, qu'ayanr apres entend
uncertain.note: sic: 'qu'ayanr' for 'qu'ayant'. Checked at 17x — the final letter is an r (shoulder, no crossbar), unlike the t of 'tant,' earlier on the same line. Transcribed as printed per §7.

uncertain.text: & comme tranſportee, ne voulant plus viute, demãda
uncertain.note: sic: 'viute' where the sense wants 'viure' (vivre). The fourth letter has a clear crossbar and a curved foot, so it is a t, not an r — a turned or wrong sort. Transcribed as printed.

uncertain.text: Ce qu'elle impetra & entre les bras de ceſte ombre ren
uncertain.note: the last word of the line is over-inked. Two vertical stems with a shoulder are visible and the counter sits high, which reads as n, and the sense requires 'ren' + 'dit' = 'rendit l'ame' on the next line. But the glyph could be read as a blotted a ('rea'). Reader B may differ. ESCALATE.

uncertain.text: voyant, dont l'amour en grec eſt appelé ἐρῶς: car du re-
uncertain.note: Greek word set in a small greek fount: epsilon with a breathing mark, rho, omega with a circumflex, final sigma — transcribed ἐρῶς (for ἔρως). The breathing over the epsilon is a small c-shaped mark; whether it is psili or dasia cannot be told at this resolution, and the accent placement is the printer's, not classical. Reader B may read ἔρως or ἐρως.
